rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> 2-year RCBD field trial at Faridkot and Abohar (2019, 2020) with measured irrigation, soil moisture and yield. Q2: Table 8 and 'Comparison of water use efficiency' section <U+2013> WUE under surface flood 57.0% vs 75.4<U+2013>83.5% under SSDF; applied water under SF 56<U+2013>110% higher than SSDI 100% ETc in 2019; irrigation water saving of 36<U+2013>54% (Faridkot) and 52<U+2013>61% (Abohar) under SSDI vs SF in 2019, 20<U+2013>50% in 2020. Q4: Tables 6 and 7 <U+2013> runoff (86<U+2013>93 mm) and deep drainage (200<U+2013>299 mm) under SF versus far lower losses under drip, which is the water-loss pathway through which drip conserves water; soil profile moisture measured with TDR profile probe.
rows.notes: Water saving derived from water-meter records and a soil water balance (TDR probe) <U+2013> treated as a single field water-balance method, so no triangulation. Only two sites, one crop, one cultivar; plot scale. Uncertainty reported only as LSD values (no SD/SE/CI). No limitations of the study stated; conditions such as 80% ETc being optimum are reported for yield rather than stated as requirements for the water-saving effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> 2-year field experiment at two stations with three replications. Q2: Table 5 and Conclusion <U+2013> SSDF at 80% ETc with 100% RDN gave 3,455 kg ha-1 SCY, 26.6% higher than surface flood (2,728 kg ha-1); SSDI 80% and 100% ETc 18.7% and 21% above SF. Q4: Tables 5<U+2013>7 and Figure 4 <U+2013> bolls per plant 23<U+2013>29% higher under SSDI than SF, biomass higher, actual crop ET measured per treatment with a linear SCY<U+2013>ETa relationship (R2 0.72<U+2013>0.98), i.e. the intermediate crop water use and yield components through which the yield gain arises were measured.
rows.notes: Yield measured by hand picking only (one method). Two sites, one crop and cultivar, plot scale. Yield at SSDI 60% ETc fell below SF, implying adequate irrigation level matters, but authors do not state this explicitly as a requirement for the yield advantage; optimum of 80% ETc with 112.5 kg N is given as a recommendation. No limitations stated. Only LSD values reported, no measure of dispersion.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> own 2-year field trial at Faridkot and Abohar comparing SSDI, SDI and surface flood. Q2: 'Effect of different treatments on water productivity indices' and Table 8 <U+2013> SSDI saved 36<U+2013>54% and 52<U+2013>61% of irrigation water over SF at the two sites in 2019 (20<U+2013>50% in 2020); WUE 76.5<U+2013>80.3% under SSDI vs 57.0% under SF; conclusion states SSDF results in significant savings of irrigation water due to lesser drainage loss. Q4: Tables 6 and 7 <U+2013> measured/estimated runoff and deep drainage much larger under SF than under sub-surface drip, the loss pathways through which SSDI conserves water.
rows.notes: Same evidence as row 1; the passage attributes water conservation to SSDI, which is the technology tested. Single field water-balance method, two sites, plot scale, no stated limitations or conditions, LSD only.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> own 2-year field experiment on cotton under SSDI, SDI and surface flood.
rows.notes: The study reports no data on weeds or weed control; it measures growth, yield, fiber quality, water productivity, NUE and economics only. Weed control is not mentioned anywhere in the results. The claim of weed-control benefits from SSDI is not supported by this study's own evidence.

notes: Full text available including all tables. Table 8 NUE rows are garbled in the text but values are recoverable. Statistics limited to LSD at p=0.05 with no SD/SE/CI; authors state no limitations of their study.
